answer: A decentralized latency atlas counters Sybil attacks by binding each agent to verifiable physical coordinates. Anchors triangulate the origin of an agent's clock signal filtered through a jade acoustic resonator using microsecond time-of-flight measurements. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of acquiring geographically separated radio hardware per identity. However, unpredictable ionospheric delays can distort flight-time calculations, spuriously rejecting legitimate agents.
